full_judgment:
2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that on 17.03.2005 the respondent Nos.1-4 filed an application under Order VI rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the plaint of Title Suit No. 218 of 2003 which was filed by their predecessor in 1984 stating, inter-alia that the defendant No. 1petitioner by filing a written statement in the said suit categorically claimed ownership of the suit property adverse to that plaintiffs-respondent Nos. 1-4. It is absolutely necessary for the plaintiffs to amend the plaint for final adjudication of the real question of ownership in the suit property. In the said petition for amendment the plaintiffs proposed that in the cause title page of the suit after the address of the defendant No. 3 the words and figure 'suit for ejectment of lessees. Suit valued at TK. 71,000.00 will be deleted and the following words and figure are to be inserted 'suit for declaration and for khas possession. Suit valued at TK. 60,00,000.00' and that in the prayer portion of the plaint the prayer No. (a) will be deleted and the following prayer shall be inserted that a decree be passed against the defendant No. 1 and in favour of the plaintiffs declaring that the plaintiffs are the sixteen annas owners of the 'B' scheduled property and that the proposed amendment for declaration of title is, merely an additional relief for necessary and appropriate relief and that the proposed amendment will not change the nature of the suit for eviction. 

 3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all material allegations contending, inter-alia, that the defendant. No. 1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 828 of 1979 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title which was converted into a suit for declaration of title and partition. The said suit is now pending before the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka at present 6th Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka wherein it is renumbered as Title Suit No. 290 of 2004. In the said suit the predecessor of the plaintiffs-respondent Nos.1-4 filed written statement on 19.03.1980 stating the plaintiff was the licensee of his mother in the suit land. Thereafter, in 1984 the predecessor of the plaintiffs-respondent Nos. 1-4 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 381 of 1984 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for ejectment of licensee against the defendant No. 1-petitioner which is now pending before the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka at present 6th Joint District Judge, Dhaka as Title Suit No. 218 of 2003. Both the suit has been continuing simultaneously, The defendant No. 1 of Title Suit No. 218 of 2003 categorically claimed ownership over the suit property firstly in 1979 through Title Suit No. 290 of 2004 and thereafter in 1985 through the written statement filed by this petitioner as defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 218 of 2003 and after about 26 years of the institution of Title Suit No. 290 of 2004 and after 21 years of the institution of the ejectment suit the present petition for amendment to the plaint of this suit praying turning this suit for ejectment of licensee into a suit for declaration of title and khas possession is barred by the law of Limitation. Since 1980 by filing written statement in Title Suit No. 290 of 2004 and since 1984 through Title Suit No. 218 of 2003 is the, licensee of the grandmother of the plaintiffs-respondent Nos.1-4 and as such, they are now estopped from raising new plea of title in accordance with the principle of law of estoppel. That from the proposed amendment petition it is clear that the plaintiffs have set up a Completely different and new case in their amendment petition. If this petition is allowed it will change the entire nature and character of the suit and the suit will convert into a suit of another new nature and character and in the name of amendment one should not he allowed to alter the fundamental character of the suit nor be allowed to turn his suit into a suit of new character and hence the petition for amendment is liable to be rejected.
